digest.headline: This week in AI and platform engineering
digest.intro: The releases that matter this week.

items.title: vLLM v0.12.0
items.summary: vLLM 0.12 adds speculative decoding for multi-modal models and drops Python 3.8. It also fixes a scheduler stall with mixed prompt lengths.
items.whyItMatters: Teams serving vision models can speed up inference, and anyone still on Python 3.8 must upgrade before moving to this release.

items.title: KServe v0.15.0
items.summary: KServe 0.15 adds an inference graph resource for chaining models and a Hugging Face runtime backed by vLLM.
items.whyItMatters: Platform teams can compose multi-model pipelines declaratively instead of writing glue services.

sources.title: vLLM v0.12.0
sources.summary: Speculative decoding now supports multi-modal models. Python 3.9 is no longer supported. The default scheduler no longer stalls when prompt lengths are mixed.

sources.title: KServe v0.15.0
sources.summary: Adds an inference graph resource for chaining models and a Hugging Face serving runtime with a vLLM backend.
